verifiedEvidence: Source and visual compared: Bedrock application architecture

The Bedrock console offers supported playground experiences for evaluating models before application integration. Runtime calls, retrieval and offline customization are separate operations. Converse provides a consistent interface for supported conversational models, while model-native invocation and feature-specific APIs have their own request formats; a single identical request is not supported for every model. Fine-tuning commonly uses prepared training data in S3 for a supported customization job.

Compare model size, context capacity, quality, latency, supported inference modes, customization options, constraints, compliance and licensing. verifiedEvidence: Source and visual compared: Choose a foundation model by workload

The source compares historical versions of Titan Text Express, Llama 2, Claude 2.1 and SDXL using context limits, features, tasks and prices. A larger context window can hold more information but does not guarantee coherent or correct use of every passage. The usable input budget depends on model limits and output reservation. For a hypothetical combined 8,000-token budget with 2,000 reserved for output, at most 6,000 remain for all input instructions, history, user content and retrieved evidence; actual model limits differ.

verifiedEvidence: Source and visual compared: Embeddings: content as vectors

Tokenization maps pieces of text to token IDs; an embedding model maps content to a numeric vector representation. Depending on the model, vectors can represent tokens, passages or other content. Dimensions capture learned features and are not generally human-readable labels. Compare query and document embeddings from a compatible model and representation space.

verifiedEvidence: Source and visual compared: Semantic similarity in embedding space

Nearest-neighbor search can use cosine similarity, dot product or a distance measure, depending on the embedding model and index. A 2D projection is only an illustration of a high-dimensional representation. Semantic similarity is useful for search, but it does not establish factual truth or authorize access to a document.
